answer: Reputation decay curve. Each identity accrues a trust score from sustained, unique interactions; the score halves when an identity stays dormant or repeats against the same counterparties, so a whisper of activity from a fresh node earns near-zero weight in matching. An attacker must sustain many parallel identities past this decay horizon, paying continuous compute and counterparty fees per node for months before any is economically usable. The cost scales with fan-out, not a one-time toll; a single sonnet of coordinated accounts costs as much as a small island of genuine operators.
